note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` covers only a high-probability PE specifically on a `vq-lung-scan` (a perfusion defect on any other scan type never counts) and a widespread metastatic pattern — a reduced ejection fraction (< 40%) is its own dedicated major-severity trigger (R-SEV-MAJOR-02), checked before the perfusion-defect actionable-finding rule and entirely independent of `hasCriticalFinding`, so it never escalates past 'urgent' follow-up.

personas.name: normal-bone-scan-complete
personas.description: A normal Tc-99m MDP bone scan for chronic low back pain with no red-flag features: symmetrical tracer uptake throughout the skeleton, no focal abnormality, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.clinicalHistory: Chronic low back pain, no red-flag features; bone scan to exclude bony metastatic disease.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous bone scan available for comparison.
state.findingsNarrative: Normal, symmetrical tracer uptake throughout the axial and appendicular skeleton. No focal areas of increased or decreased uptake.
state.impression: Normal bone scan; no scintigraphic evidence of bony metastatic disease.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further nuclear medicine follow-up required for this indication.

expected.recommendedAction: No specific imaging follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: No abnormal structured findings on an interpretable examination; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: abnormal-reduced-ejection-fraction-major-not-critical-complete
personas.description: A gated myocardial perfusion SPECT for exertional chest pain shows a moderate reversible inferolateral perfusion defect on stress with near-complete resolution at rest, and gated analysis shows a reduced left-ventricular ejection fraction of 32%: the ejection-fraction threshold (< 40%) is a dedicated major-severity rule checked before the perfusion-defect actionable-finding rule, and a perfusion defect on a myocardial-perfusion study (unlike a high-probability PE on a V/Q lung scan) is never a `hasCriticalFinding` trigger, so this escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, never critical-alert; report complete — expect abnormal classification + major severity (reportingCategory reduced-ejection-fraction) + 100% completeness + urgent follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.radiopharmaceutical: Tc-99m tetrofosmin, stress and rest gated SPECT, 350 MBq each.
state.clinicalHistory: Exertional chest pain and breathlessness; gated myocardial perfusion SPECT to assess for inducible ischaemia and left-ventricular function.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous myocardial perfusion scan on file.
state.findingsNarrative: A moderate-sized reversible perfusion defect is seen in the inferolateral wall on stress imaging, with near-complete resolution at rest, consistent with inducible ischaemia. Gated analysis shows globally reduced left-ventricular systolic function.
state.impression: Reversible inferolateral perfusion defect with reduced left-ventricular ejection fraction (32%), consistent with inducible ischaemia and impaired systolic function.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to cardiology for consideration of coronary angiography and heart-failure work-up given the reduced ejection fraction.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent clinical review and expedite onward referral.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured findings are present; classified as abnormal.
Left-ventricular ejection fraction is markedly reduced (< 40 %); abnormality severity graded major.
Major abnormality present; follow-up urgency graded urgent.

flags.description: A perfusion defect or photopenic area is present and may warrant urgent referral.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider urgent referral to the appropriate specialist team.

personas.name: critical-widespread-bone-metastases-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: A bone scan shows multiple, widespread foci of markedly increased tracer uptake throughout the axial skeleton and proximal long bones, in keeping with a widespread metastatic pattern ('superscan'): a widespread metastatic pattern auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history, comparison, and impression sections are not yet completed while urgent oncology review is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Multiple, widespread foci of markedly increased tracer uptake are seen throughout the axial skeleton (skull, spine, ribs, pelvis) and proximal long bones, in keeping with a widespread metastatic pattern ("superscan").
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the referring oncology team immediately; urgent oncology review being arranged.
